name: Illinois

law.summary: The 42 Chicago-area CSO permits (Chicago, MWRD and the TARP suburbs) are Great Lakes Basin CSO permits: under 40 CFR 122.38 they must notify the public electronically within 4 hours of becoming aware of a CSO; MWRD does this by email/SMS alerts and a map for itself and the suburbs. Downstate CSO permits carry a permit notification condition (NMC #8, no deadline found). No Illinois statute or rule requiring public notice of SSOs or bypasses was found; those go to Illinois EPA within 24 hours.

citations.title: Public notification requirements for CSO discharges to the Great Lakes Basin
citations.quote: As soon as possible, but no later than four (4) hours after becoming aware by monitoring, modeling or other means that a CSO discharge has occurred, the Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall provide public notification of CSO discharges. The Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee shall provide public notification of CSO discharges electronically, such as by text, email, social media alerts to subscribers or by posting a notice on its public access website
citations.who: Great Lakes Basin CSO permittee (42 Chicago-area permits per EPA)
citations.channel: text, email, social media or website; signs at outfalls and access areas; local health department within 4 hours

cso.notification_practice: Cook County: MWRD alerts by email/SMS (Smart911), a daily 'Possible CSO Events' map and a per-outfall CSO Event Synopsis Report; suburbs rely on MWRD. Downstate: SOBE rows for some permits (Pekin 115 CSO rows); own channels mostly not found or not searched. 45 of 46 checked CSO permits rely on MWRD channels (only MWRD itself runs them); the other 74 downstate permits were checked only against SOBE.

readiness.rationale: EPA's daily SOBE tables carry 1,687 Illinois events with start, end, volume and coordinates, so the statewide feed exists and is already ingested for other states. Latency is a median 3 days, hence 'delayed'. Cook County CSOs are missing from SOBE and need a second ingester: the MWRD CSO Event Synopsis Report (per-outfall open/close times) plus the Possible CSO Events layer as a same-day signal, which would make the Chicago area 'Dated reports'.

owner_questions: Subscribe to MWRD Smart911 CSO alerts (email) so the 4-hour notices can be timed against the map and the synopsis report?
Accept a session-based scraper for the MWRD CSO Event Synopsis Report (ASP.NET ReportViewer CSV export), or ask MWRD for a direct feed?
Show downstate CSO permits with no SOBE CSO rows as 'No public reports' or wait for an ECHO DMR check?
surprise: Illinois is the one heavy-CSO state where EPA's own event tables already work statewide (1,687 events, all with coordinates), yet they miss Chicago entirely: the City, MWRD and 37 suburban CSO permits file nothing there, and the Chicago record lives in an MWRD report server with per-outfall gate open and close times back to 2016.
